AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
“In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability related modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the City Clerk’s office at 310-952-1720 prior to the meeting.” (Government Code Section 54954.2)

CALL TO ORDER: CITY COUNCIL

ROLL CALL: Others present: Sharon Landers, Sunny Soltani, Dave Roberts, Kevin Kennedy, Mike Whittaker, Saied Naaseh, Tarik Rahmani, Monica Cooper and Captain Skeen. 

Mayor Robles made comments about the City's Drive Thru Testing site.

LDH offered comments related to testing site. She noted residents concerns about having to provide their personal information to get tested. 

CM Landers noted that the information provided is similar to a patient visiting a doctors office for the first time. 

Discussion ensued about billing. Mayor confirmed that no resident will be required to pay their deductible. 

Council member Hicks spoke about mobile home park residents that do not have access to upload copies of their identification and personal information. He directed CM to reach out to residents of mobile home parks advising them of the senior hotline number for testing information. 

CM Landers noted she will mail all mobile home park residents a letter. 

MPT Dear noted his experience visiting the testing site. In addition to the application being a little problematic for residents.

**ORAL COMMUNICATIONS** City Clerk read public comments

DISCUSSION: (Item 1) Captain Skeen announced: Emergency Blood Drive 5/29 at the Carson Station 10:00am - 4:00pm; Spoke about resources for those dealing with social isolation and mental health issues related to Stay Home orders. Crime Statistics. 

Council member Hicks inquired about how would people with drivers license and identifications that are expiring soon, handle getting them updated with Department of Motor Vehicles being closed. 

Captain Skeen acknowledged that because of the shot down, the public should still keep their expired Identification/Driver License with them at all times. Courtesies are being offered during the state of emergency. 

Council member Hilton spoke about loitering about the city particular at CSUDH and Dales Liquor Store. Captain Skeen addressed his concerns. 

MPT Dear inquired about homelessness  - captain skeen addressed his question. 

David Roberts introduced Dr. Camille Babaie 

Dr. Camille Babaie Medical Director for US Health Fairs addressed fed mandate requiring all insurance companies cover the cost for COVID-19 testing without deductibles for everyone. In addition, she spoke about the standard information required to verify insurance information and identify that the person is who he say he is. She spoke about providing testing for people with logistics barriers - they will go into the homes of those individuals. The difference between saliva testing (pending CDC approval) versus nasal swabs. She noted that demographic data/information will be made available to public as they gather the information. She recommended spreading out employee testing times. 

LDH inquired about how soon a plan can be put together for mobile testing sites for the senior homes in the city. In addition to asking about antibodies. 

Dr. Babaie noted that US Health Fairs can work with staff to get a plan in place right a way. In addition, she addressed her question about testing for antibodies. 

Mayor and City Council thanked Dr. Babaie and US Health Fairs for assisting to make the Carson Drive Thru testing site into fruition. 

Council member Hilton also noted the partnership with Herbalife for providing the drive thru testing site workers with protein bars and snacks to get them through the day. 

ACM Roberts gave a status on testing kits provided during todays testing. He publicly thanked IKEA for providing Tupperware for their testing equipment while providing home visits for testing.  

Mayor Robles noted that the City has provided over 900 tests to residents for the first two days.

LDH inquired about how information was distributed to the public advising of the testing site. Roberts noted social media, city website, plans to mail a letter to residents, and announcement on bill board sites.  

City Manager Landers noted that through research it was identified that only one person in the city's different senior homes have tested positive and believe this is a testament to how well the senior homes are being taken care of.

She introduced Terri Billups representative of Small Business Administration 

Terri Billups spoke about the process for small businesses to go about accessing SBA funding through lenders.  

Council member Hilton inquired about SBA checking business owner personal credit.
